claim: Senigallia's seafront is 13 km of very fine golden sand, soft as velvet, giving it the name Spiaggia di Velluto; it holds Blue Flag certification continuously since 1997 and has over 60 lifeguard stations with shallow, current-free water ideal for families.
quote: thirteen kilometres of very fine golden sand, as soft and light as velvet

claim: The Spiaggia di Velluto nickname comes from the exceptionally fine, soft sand that feels like walking on velvet, a feature distinguishing it from other Adriatic beaches.
quote: the velvet beach of Senigallia owes its name to the very fine sand that resembles a soft velvet carpet between the city and the sea

claim: The Rotonda a Mare is an elegant rationalist-style seaside venue built in the 1930s by engineer Enrico Cardelli, with a covered platform and raised terrace; it peaked as a glamorous entertainment temple in the 1950s-60s, reopened in 2006 after a fire, and now hosts exhibitions and events free of charge June-September.
quote: typically rationalist... a platform with a large covered canopy and a large raised terrace, created by engineer Enrico Cardelli

claim: The Rotonda a Mare originated as a Belle Epoque wooden hydrotherapy platform; the decision to build it was made January 30 1932 and it was inaugurated July 18 1933, becoming the symbol of Senigallia.
quote: la decisione definitiva di costruire la Rotonda a Mare... fu inaugurata il 18 luglio 1933

claim: Senigallia's 13 km seafront mixes equipped beach clubs (stabilimenti / bagni) with free public beaches (spiaggia libera), spread across the Ponente (west) and Levante (east) sides on lungomari Mameli, Marconi, Da Vinci, Alighieri and Italia.
quote: Tutti gli stabilimenti balneari a Senigallia

claim: At a Senigallia stabilimento in 2026 an umbrella plus two loungers averages about 159 euros per week (Aug 2-8, first four rows), one of the more affordable Italian resorts with only a 0.6% increase over 2025.
quote: Senigallia... 159 euro per ombrellone e due lettini... aumento dello 0,6%

claim: You can cycle along nearly the entire 13 km of Senigallia coast on dedicated bike paths, including an 8 km route connecting the centre to Marzocca via the eastern waterfront, part of the Adriatic Cycle Route (Ciclovia Adriatica).
quote: percorrere in bicicletta quasi tutti i 13 km di costa su pista ciclabile

claim: Lungomare Goffredo Mameli is a vibrant seafront promenade stretching for kilometres, ideal for morning jogs or strolls, lined with beachwear shops, souvenir stalls and eateries.
quote: a vibrant seafront promenade that stretches for kilometers, offering an ideal setting for morning jogs or leisurely strolls

claim: Rocca Roveresca opens daily 8:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. (ticket office closes 7:00 p.m.), closed Dec 25 and Jan 1; full ticket EUR5, reduced EUR2 (ages 18-25), under-18 free.
quote: From Monday to Sunday 8.30 a.m. - 7.30 p.m. ... Standard ticket: EUR5.00 ... Reduced (ages 18-25): EUR2.00 ... closed on December 25th and January 1st.

claim: The Rocca Roveresca was rebuilt into a Renaissance fortress under Giovanni della Rovere in the late 15th century by architects Luciano Laurana and Baccio Pontelli, also serving as a noble palace and seat of an artillery academy founded by Guidubaldo della Rovere in 1533.
quote: Giovanni della Rovere commissioning renowned architects Luciano Laurana and Baccio Pontelli to reconstruct the fortress into a Renaissance masterpiece ... seat of an artillery academy founded by Guidubaldo della Rovere in 1533.

claim: The Foro Annonario, a circular neoclassical brick market designed by Senigallia architect Pietro Ghinelli in 1834, has a portico of 24 Doric columns, hosts a daily fruit-and-vegetable market with food and wine shops, and now also holds the Antonelliana Library and Municipal Archives.
quote: Pietro Ghinelli designed this neoclassical structure in 1834 ... a complex of 24 columns with Doric-style capitals ... houses a daily fruit and vegetable market ... now hosts the Antonelliana Library and Municipal Archives.

claim: The Foro Annonario was conceived as an urban backdrop for the river axis parallel to the eighteenth-century Portici Ercolani, with its construction spanning roughly 1810 to 1847.
quote: the idea of creating a new square as an urban backdrop for the river axis, parallel to the eighteenth-century Portici Ercolani

claim: The Portici Ercolani run along the right bank of the Misa river as 126 Istrian-stone arches, designed by Monsignor Giuseppe Ercolani in the mid-18th century on the order of Pope Benedict XIV as the venue for the Fiera Franca trade fair, replacing the old fortress walls.
quote: 126 magnificent Istrian-stone arcades ... named after Monsignor Giuseppe Ercolani (1677-1759), who designed them in the mid of the 18th century upon order of Pope Benedict XIV ... as the celebration venue for the famous Fiera Franca (Trade Fair).

claim: The Portici Ercolani still host trade, filling with stalls for the St. Augustine fair (Aug 28-30) and every Thursday for the weekly open-air market; a scenic walk runs from the Vecchia Filanda in Piazza Garibaldi toward the Rione Porto harbour district.
quote: every Thursday of the year for the weekly open air market ... A suggested walk under the silent arcades of Portici Ercolani starts from Vecchia Filanda (Old Spinning Mill) in Piazza Garibaldi towards Rione Porto

claim: Palazzetto Baviera, overlooking Piazza del Duca, was built for Giovanni Giacomo Baviera (Giovanni della Rovere's uncle) and its main floor holds ceilings entirely decorated in stucco by Federico Brandani of Urbino across five themed rooms (Imperial Rome, Republican Rome, the Iliad, Hercules, the Old Testament).
quote: ceilings entirely decorated in stucco by Federico Brandani from Urbino ... The ceilings of the five rooms (of Imperial Rome, Republican Rome, the Iliad, Hercules, the Old Testament) are undoubtedly the greatest expression of Federico Brandani's work.

claim: Piazza del Duca, named for Giovanni della Rovere and once used for parades and military exercises, holds the 1596 Fontana delle Anatre (also called fonte del Duca or dei Leoni) in pink marble with bronze decorations, set off-center because of the parade ground.
quote: la beautiful Fontana delle Anatre ... del 1596 in pink marble with bronze decorations ... used as a place for parades and military exercises ... the Fontana delle Anatre (or dei Leoni) is off-center with respect to the plan.

claim: Senigallia's Duomo, the Cathedral of San Pietro Apostolo, was built 1762-1790 to a design by Paolo Posi on a former Jesuit church, with a neoclassical two-order facade (Doric below, Ionic above) remade in 1877 by Augusto Innocenti and financed by Senigallia-born Pope Pius IX.
quote: built according to the project of architect Paolo Posi ... between 1762 and 1790 ... The facade, in neoclassical style with two superimposed orders (Doric in the lower part, Ionic in the upper), was remade in 1877, based on a design by Augusto Innocenti ... financed by Pope Pio IX, who originated from Senigallia.

claim: MUSINF holds ~1,700 works from 50+ artists and a complete anthology of 250 photos donated by Mario Giacomelli, including the Scanno and 'Io non ho mani' series, plus the Misa Photographic School founded by Giuseppe Cavalli in 1950s Senigallia.
quote: approximately 1,700 works donated by over 50 major artists ... a complete anthology of two hundred fifty photos ... Misa Photographic School, established in Senigallia during the 1950s, with particular emphasis on founder Giuseppe Cavalli and Giacomelli

claim: The original MUSINF location is closed for renovation; its collections have been transferred to Palazzo del Duca, with admission free.
quote: Currently closed for renovations. Collections have been transferred to Palazzo del Duca. Admission is free.

claim: Palazzo del Duca shows a permanent Mario Giacomelli collection plus rotating photography exhibitions; in summer 2026 Palazzo del Duca and Palazzetto Baviera open Thu-Sun with evening hours, and a Rocca Roveresca ticket earns a discount on the civic museums.
quote: Palazzo del Duca houses a permanent collection of works by Mario Giacomelli ... An entrance ticket to Rocca Roveresca allows a discount on admission to the civic museums Palazzo del Duca and Palazzetto Baviera

claim: Palazzo Mastai is the 16th-century birthplace of Pope Pius IX (born 13 May 1792); the first-floor Museo Pio IX holds relics of his life including a cycle of twenty biblical canvases by Giovanni Anastasi, and entry is free.
quote: the birthplace of Pope Pius IX (Giovanni Maria Mastai Ferretti) on May 13, 1792 ... a cycle of twenty canvases with biblical subjects ... Free entry

claim: The Pinacoteca Diocesana, in the bishop's palace on Piazza Garibaldi (opened 1992), centers on Federico Barocci's 'Madonna of the Rosary and Saint Dominic' (1588-1592) plus works by Andrea Lilli, Donducci and Ramazzani; entry is free.
quote: The collection's most celebrated piece is The Madonna of the Rosary and Saint Dominic by Federico Barocci (1535-1612) ... Admission: Free entry

claim: The Area Archeologica e Museo 'La Fenice' was closed to the public until 1 March 2026 for restoration coordinated by the Superintendence of Archaeology.
quote: The Archaeological Area and Museum La Fenice will remain closed to the public until March 1, 2026 for maintenance and restoration work

claim: La Fenice is a museumized excavation beneath the modern theatre showing Roman buildings (2nd-3rd c. AD) at the cardo/decumanus crossing of ancient Sena, walkable a few metres below ground.
quote: one of the few places in Italy where it's possible to admire both the remains of Roman buildings together with finds recovered on site ... the intersection between a 'cardo' ... and a 'decumanus'

claim: Typical museum-weekend hours: Casa Museo Pio IX Thu 9-14 and Sat 15-20 (free); Pinacoteca Diocesana daily 9-12 and 16-21; Palazzo del Duca and Palazzetto Baviera Thu-Sun with paid entry.
quote: Casa Museo Pio IX: 'giovedì dalle 9.00 alle 14.00 e sabato dalle 15.00 alle 20.00' ... Pinacoteca Diocesana: 'tutti i giorni dalle 9.00 alle 12.00 e dalle 16.00 alle 21.00'

claim: Brodetto alla senigalliese is the local signature fish stew made with 13 types of fish (mantis shrimp, mullet, gurnard, sole, cuttlefish, monkfish, etc.) cooked slowly without stirring in tomato, vinegar and Verdicchio, served with garlic toast.
quote: The authentic recipe calls for 13 different types of fish... combined in a sauce of cherry tomatoes, peeled tomatoes, olive oil, onion, garlic, vinegar, and Verdicchio wine... served very hot with slices of toasted bread with garlic.

claim: Beyond the two starred restaurants, casual Senigallia options include Vicoletto da Michele, La Tartana, Da Carlo and Al Cuoco di Bordo, and a full fish dinner (fried olives, brodetto or passatelli, fish, dessert) typically costs 28-42 euros.
quote: famous restaurants ULIASSI and MADONNINA DEL PESCATORE... along with many others both by the sea and inland including Vicoletto da Michele, La Tartana, Da Carlo, and Al Cuoco di Bordo... A complete dinner... costs between 28 and 42 euros.

claim: Gelateria Paolo Brunelli is Senigallia's celebrated gelato maker, ranked among Italy's best, with signature flavors like Crema Brunelli (cream, caramelized hazelnut, chocolate, Madagascar vanilla) and Portonovo (bitter Campari jelly).
quote: Paolo Brunelli... among the absolute best in the gelato world... signature Crema Brunelli, which combines cream, caramelized hazelnuts, chocolate, and vanilla from Madagascar. Other notable flavors are Portonovo, featuring bitter Campari jelly.

claim: Other recommended Senigallia gelaterias beyond Brunelli include Puro & Bio (unusual combos like melon and lavender) and Gelateria Papaya 2.0 (generous portions).
quote: Puro & Bio, which offers an impressive array of unique flavors with standout combinations like melon and lavender, and Gelateria Papaya 2.0, which offers a delightful array of flavors with generous portions.

claim: For aperitivo and wine, Senigallia's pedestrian centre offers wine bars including Saltatappo Vinoteca (strong local selection, good value), Galli Enoteca (historic-centre wine shop running tastings and winery tours) and Saffi Caffe (natural wines).
quote: Saltatappo Vinoteca - A charming wine bar in the heart of Senigallia... Galli Enoteca... reference point for all wine lovers... organises evenings, tastings and winery tours... Saffi Caffe... selection of natural wines.

claim: Vincisgrassi, a rich layered egg-pasta bake (ancestor of lasagna) with mixed-meat and chicken-giblet ragu and bechamel, is a must inland Marche pasta found on Senigallia tables.
quote: Vincisgrassi is one of the symbolic dishes of the Marchigian hinterland... egg pasta rolled out thinly and arranged in layers, alternated with a flavorful and full-bodied ragu, often prepared with mixed meat and chicken giblets... All the tables of the inhabitants of Senigallia... are absolutely laid with... renowned vincisgrassi.

claim: Marche street-food staples to try include olive all'ascolana (hand-pitted Ascolana olives stuffed with mixed meat, breaded and fried) and crescia sfogliata, a lard-rich rolled flatbread from the Pesaro-Urbino area.
quote: Olive ascolane... pitted by hand and stuffed with a mixed meat filling... breaded and fried... a true icon of Marchigian street food... Crescia sfogliata is a typical specialty of the provinces of Pesaro and Urbino... emblem of local street food.

claim: Moscioli are wild mussels growing naturally on the rocks between Ancona and Sirolo on the nearby Conero Riviera, a Slow Food Presidium since 2004, celebrated at the June 'Mosciolando' festival in Portonovo.
quote: The Portonovo Wild Mussel is a Slow Food presidium since 2004. Moscioli are wild mussels growing naturally in the stretch of sea between Pietralacroce (Ancona) and Sirolo... A festival dedicated to this specialty, Mosciolando, takes place in Portonovo in June.

claim: As of the 2025 season Slow Food Italia suspended the moscioli Presidium and asked the Ministry of Agriculture to block fishing of the species because the wild-mussel population is in steep decline, so visitors may not find authentic Portonovo moscioli.
quote: Slow Food Italia has officially suspended the Presidio and has submitted a request to the Ministry of Agriculture to block fishing of this species for the entire 2025 season. The mosciolo population is in constant decline.

claim: Highly rated casual seafood spots in Senigallia per diner reviews include Bruna Bistro, La Lampara and Il Mare in Terrazza, serving fritto misto, grilled sardoncini, shellfish and brodetto alla marchigiana with local Verdicchio.
quote: top-rated fish and seafood restaurants include Bruna Bistro, La Lampara, and Il Mare in Terrazza... Typical dishes include sardoncini scottadito (grilled sardines), fried fish, brodetto, mussels, clams, and sea snails.

claim: Summer Jamboree 2026 (26th edition) runs 31 July to 9 August 2026, with 31 July as a pre-festival day.
quote: The festival runs July 31 - August 9, 2026, with July 31 designated as a prefestival event.

claim: Summer Jamboree is Europe's largest 1940s-50s American music and culture festival, covering Rock'n'Roll, Swing, Rockabilly, R&B, Doo-Wop, Hillbilly, Country and Boogie Woogie with concerts, social dancing (Lindy Hop, Boogie Woogie, Balboa, Jive), vintage markets, vintage cars and burlesque.
quote: Rock'n'Roll and Swing in all their forms: Rockabilly, Rhythm'n'Blues, Doo-Wop, Hillbilly, Country & Western Swing, Dixieland, Boogie Woogie and more.

claim: Summer Jamboree has drawn record crowds of around 400,000 presences over its ~10-day run, packing the town.
quote: Oltre 400.000 presenze a Senigallia per il Summer Jamboree

claim: The 2025 (25th) edition set new attendance records with the Rotonda a Mare sold out for ten nights.
quote: Summer Jamboree, l'edizione 25 da record. Migliaia di visitatori, Rotonda sold out per dieci serate

claim: CaterRaduno, the Radio2 Caterpillar fan rally hosted in Senigallia since 2007 (held in late June), left the town: it moved to Pesaro from 2022 after roughly twenty years.
quote: Ora è ufficiale: il Caterraduno dice addio a Senigallia, dal 2022 si trasferisce a Pesaro

claim: CaterRaduno was a week of live radio shows, concerts, guests, civil-battle talks and humour staged on the Velvet Beach in June.
quote: a week full of information, civil battles and biting humour ... concerts, guests, live radio shows, entertainment and fun on the Velvet Beach

claim: Pane Nostrum, Senigallia's international bread/leavened-products festival, is held at the Foro Annonario in the historic centre in late September (20-23 September 2026).
quote: Senigallia Pane Nostrum Bread Festival 2026

claim: The Fiera di Sant'Agostino, a centuries-old market fair, fills the historic centre at the end of August (27-30 August) with over 500 exhibitors plus local-producer and organic sections.
quote: Fiera di S.Agostino

claim: The Festival del Cinema di Senigallia, run by the Confluenze association at the San Rocco Auditorium, takes place in October (12th edition 10-18 October 2025; 13th edition slated for October 2026).
quote: Si è conclusa con successo la XII edizione del Festival del Cinema di Senigallia

claim: The best time to visit Senigallia is May to September, with July-August the sunniest and liveliest (August averaging ~30C max) but also the busiest and priciest; late May-June and early September offer better value.
quote: The best time to visit Senigallia ... is during the summer months of June, July, and August ... August has an average maximum temperature of 30°C and is the warmest month

claim: The Frasassi Caves at Genga are about 50 km (roughly one hour's drive) from Senigallia.
quote: The Frasassi Caves are located in the territory of Genga, in the province of Ancona, and are only 50 km from Senigallia.

claim: The Frasassi Caves classic guided tour lasts 75 minutes over a 1,500-metre accessible path at a constant 14°C, so visitors should bring a pullover and non-slip shoes.
quote: Cave visits last 75 minutes. ... 1,500 metres ... The temperature inside is a constant 14 °C.

claim: Corinaldo is about 12 miles (roughly 20 minutes by car) from Senigallia.
quote: The driving distance between Corinaldo and Senigallia is 12 miles, taking approximately 20 minutes to drive.

claim: Mondavio's Rocca Roveresca, built 1482-1492 for Giovanni della Rovere lord of Senigallia and designed by Francesco di Giorgio Martini with an octagonal keep, survives in excellent condition having never been besieged.
quote: built between 1482 and 1492 at the behest of Giovanni della Rovere, lord of Senigallia ... octagonal-shaped keep ... having never suffered attacks or sieges.

claim: Corinaldo, with its intact walls and famous Pozzo della Polenta well at the top of a roughly 100-step staircase, pairs well with Mondavio for a single day trip.
quote: Corinaldo boasts intact walls and its famous Pozzo della Polenta. The Scalinata del Pozzo della Polenta is an absolute must-see, with about 100-step staircase.

claim: Urbino is about 44 miles (roughly 50-55 minutes) by car from Senigallia.
quote: The driving distance between Urbino and Senigallia is 44 miles, taking approximately 52 minutes to drive.

claim: Urbino's Palazzo Ducale, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998 commissioned by Federico da Montefeltro, houses the Galleria Nazionale delle Marche with Piero della Francesca's Flagellation and Madonna di Senigallia, and Urbino is Raphael's birthplace.
quote: The Ducal Palace is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998 ... Galleria Nazionale delle Marche ... Piero della Francesca's 'Flagellation' and 'Madonna of Senigallia' ... Urbino ... the birthplace of Raphael.

claim: The Conero Riviera town of Numana is about 32 km (roughly 38 minutes by car) from Senigallia.
quote: It takes approximately 38 min to drive from Senigallia to Numana.

claim: The Conero Riviera's main resorts are Sirolo, Numana, Marcelli and Portonovo, with Sirolo perched 125 m above the sea and beaches including Urbani, Sassi Neri, San Michele and Due Sorelle.
quote: Sirolo, an old village in a picturesque position 125 metres above the sea, is famous for its small, charming beaches - Urbani, Sassi Neri, San Michele and Due Sorelle.

claim: Gradara is about 38 miles (roughly 36 minutes, mostly motorway) by road from Senigallia.
quote: The distance from Gradara to Senigallia is 38 miles by road including 32 miles on motorways, and the road takes approximately 36 minutes.

claim: Gradara's medieval fortress, ringed by a double line of walls (the outer wall nearly 800 m long), is tied to the Dante's Inferno legend of Paolo and Francesca.
quote: protected by two walls, the outermost of which extends for almost 800 meters ... the legend of Paolo and Francesca ... in the fifth canto of the Inferno.

claim: Jesi is about 22 km from Senigallia, reachable by train in as little as 32 minutes (typically with one change).
quote: around 26 trains per day running between Jesi and Senigallia ... the 14 miles (22 km) journey. It can take as little as 32 minutes on the fastest services ... requiring a minimum of 1 change.

claim: Jesi is the birthplace of Emperor Frederick II of Swabia (born 26 Dec 1194) and the home of the Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC/DOCG wine.
quote: Emperor Federico II of Swabia was born on December 26, 1194 ... Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi wine, one of the most famous and well-known DOC wines of the Marche region.
